segments.zh: 各位英语学习者，大家好。

segments.en: And today, we are going to be teaching you a very important technique, especially for the guys if you want to have good luck with the ladies, right?
segments.zh: 今天，我们将教你一个非常重要的技术，特别是如果你想和女士们一起祝你好运的话，对吧？

segments.en: Well, today's lesson is called that's flattering.
segments.zh: 好吧，今天的课程被称为讨人喜欢。

segments.en: So we are going to be teaching you how to flatter someone.
segments.zh: 所以我们将教你如何奉承某人。

segments.en: So what does it mean to flatter someone?
segments.zh: 那么奉承一个人是什么意思呢？

segments.en: Well, basically, you're going to be giving compliments and you're going to make that person feel good about themselves.
segments.zh: 好吧，基本上，你会给予赞美，你会让那个人对自己感觉良好。

segments.en: Now, before we get on with this flattering lesson, we need to look at some vocabulary in Vocabulary Preview.

segments.en: So it's that final exam in order to finally become a lawyer.

segments.en: So now we have these two words that we're going to listen to in the dialogue.
segments.zh: 所以现在我们有了这两个词，我们将在对话中聆听。

segments.en: And now let's listen to two people as they flatter each other in our dialogue.
segments.zh: 现在让我们听两个人在我们的对话中互相奉承。

segments.en: It's been such a long time.

segments.zh: 的确，已经有一段时间了。

segments.en: I love what you've done with your hair.
I went to that hair salon you told me about, but enough about me.
segments.zh: 我去了你推荐的那家美发店。先不说我了。

segments.en: God, you haven't aged a day.
Well, I've been watching what I eat, and I work out three times a week.
segments.zh: 我一直注意饮食，每周锻炼三次。

segments.en: By the way, I heard your son recently graduated.
segments.zh: 顺便说一句，我听说你儿子最近毕业了。

segments.en: My little Paul is finally a doctor.
segments.zh: 我家小保罗终于当医生了。

segments.en: They grow up so fast, you know.
segments.zh: 他们长得太快了，你知道的。

segments.en: He is such a handsome guy.
He gets his looks from his mother, of course.
segments.zh: 他长得像他妈妈，当然帅。

segments.en: I heard she passed the bar exam and married recently.
segments.zh: 我听说她最近通过了律师资格考试，还结婚了。

segments.en: She had a beautiful wedding in Cozumel, Mexico, and we all attended.
segments.zh: 她在墨西哥科苏梅尔办了一场很美的婚礼，我们都去了。

segments.en: I hope my Paul is lucky enough to find a girl like that someday.
segments.zh: 我希望我的保罗有一天能找到这样的女孩。

segments.en: Well, it's been great talking to you, but I have to get going.
segments.zh: 跟你聊天真开心，可我得走了。

segments.en: We'll catch up soon, maybe over coffee.
segments.zh: 改天约着喝咖啡，好好聊聊。

segments.en: I cannot stand that woman or her obnoxious daughter.
segments.zh: 我真受不了那个女人，还有她那讨人厌的女儿。

segments.en: All right, so this is your typical, normal, everyday behavior that women show to each other, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，这是女性对彼此表现出的典型、正常的日常行为，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah, I think it's very common.
It's very hard to argue against this because I think everyone does it, or at least you've heard maybe your mother or your son talk to her friends like this, right?
segments.zh: 很难反驳这一点，因为我认为每个人都这样做，或者至少你听说过你的母亲或你的儿子可能会这样和她的朋友交谈，对吧？

segments.en: So pretend you like a person who you actually hate.
segments.zh: 所以假装你喜欢一个你真正讨厌的人。

segments.en: I don't know what you're doing to me now.
segments.zh: 我不知道你现在对我做了什么。

segments.en: But we can take a look at some of this great language, very rich language that we found in this dialogue in Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 但我们可以看看我们在 Fluency Builder 的对话中发现的一些伟大的语言，非常丰富的语言。

segments.zh: 在第一个中，我们将专注于您可以用来奉承某人的语言。

segments.en: In the very first part of the dialogue, we heard Valerie say, I love what you've done with your hair.
segments.zh: 在对话的第一部分，我们听到瓦莱丽说，我喜欢你对头发所做的一切。

segments.en: I love what you've done with your hair.
I love what you've done with.
I love what you've done with.
Okay, so if somebody says this, basically they're saying, I like the change you made.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以如果有人这么说，基本上他们是在说，我喜欢你所做的改变。

segments.en: And change not only to your hair, right?
So I love what you've done with your new house.
segments.zh: 所以我喜欢你对新房子所做的一切。

segments.en: Or I can say, I love what you've done with your garden.
segments.zh: 或者我可以说，我喜欢你对花园所做的一切。

segments.en: So something that you've changed, you can use this phrase for.
segments.zh: 所以你已经改变的东西，你可以使用这个短语。

segments.en: And in this case, it's her hair.
segments.zh: 在这种情况下，这是她的头发。

segments.en: So she is complimenting her on her hair.

segments.en: We also heard Darlene say, you haven't aged a day.
segments.zh: 我们还听到达琳说，你一天都没有变老。

segments.en: So now she is saying that she hasn't gotten any older.
segments.zh: 所以现在她说她没有变老。

segments.en: To age is to get older.

segments.zh: 所以这是告诉别人你看起来很棒的一种非常常见的方式。

segments.en: So then they talk about their kids and they're talking about the sun and they, and Valerie says he's such a handsome guy.
segments.zh: 所以他们谈论他们的孩子，他们谈论的是太阳和他们，瓦莱丽说他是一个如此英俊的人。

segments.en: He is such a handsome guy.
He is such a handsome guy.

segments.zh: 所以这个结构很重要，因为现在我可以改变形容词，我说他很聪明。

segments.en: He is such an intelligent guy.
segments.zh: 他是一个如此聪明的人。

segments.en: And then this is such a good day.

segments.en: I love what you've done with and he is such a, and let's listen to some examples.

segments.zh: 我们喜欢你在这个地方所做的一切。

segments.en: I love what you've done with your hair.
Such a nice color on you.
I love what you've done with this space.
segments.zh: 我喜欢你在这个空间所做的一切。

segments.en: I really like how those two phrases can fit together.
segments.zh: 我真的很喜欢这两个短语如何组合在一起。

segments.en: Yeah, they are very good and now you can use them together or separately like in the dialogue.
segments.zh: 是的，它们非常好，现在您可以像在对话中一样使用它们或单独使用它们。

segments.en: Now let's move to our final flattering phrase.
segments.zh: 现在让我们进入我们最后的讨人喜欢的短语。

segments.en: Valerie says that Darlene's son gets his looks from his mother.
segments.zh: 瓦莱丽说达琳的儿子从他的母亲那里得到了他的眼神。

segments.en: She says he gets his looks from his mother, of course.
segments.zh: 她说他当然是从他母亲那里得到的。

segments.en: So when she says he gets his looks from, she is saying his appearance.
segments.zh: 所以当她说他从中得到他的样子时，她是在说他的外表。

segments.en: His positive appearance, his good appearance.
segments.zh: 他积极的外表，他的好外表。

segments.en: So now we can change the noun and I can say he gets his intelligence from his father.
segments.zh: 所以现在我们可以改变名词，我可以说他从父亲那里得到了他的智慧。

segments.en: And then he gets his beautiful singing voice from his mother.
segments.zh: 然后他从他的母亲那里得到了他优美的歌声。

segments.en: So now typically you would say his mother, his father or maybe one of the grandparents, right?
segments.zh: 所以现在通常你会说他的母亲、他的父亲或祖父母之一，对吧？

segments.en: But you wouldn't say he gets his good looks from his brother.
segments.zh: 但你不会说他从他的兄弟那里得到了他的美貌。

segments.zh: 好吧，和你聊天真是太好了，但我必须开始了。

segments.en: It's been such a long time.
It's been such a long time.
It's been such a long time.

segments.en: Let's take a look at the first part, by the way.

segments.en: So this is a way to connect two different ideas or to start a new topic.
segments.zh: 因此，这是连接两个不同想法或开始新主题的一种方式。

segments.en: And now when she says, I heard your son recently graduated.
segments.zh: 现在当她说，我听说你儿子最近毕业了。

segments.en: So we use this phrase, I heard, when we've got information that we're not sure about.
segments.zh: 所以当我们得到我们不确定的信息时，我们使用了这个短语。

segments.en: And also you are demonstrating interest about a certain topic or a news event that you would like to know about.
segments.zh: 您还表现出对您想了解的某个主题或新闻事件的兴趣。

segments.en: And so basically you're asking the other person, tell me about this.
